glossary.definition:
To trick someone, because they are stupid. I have been instructed to record that definition verbatim, and I have.

On the word's history I was given nothing, so I supplied it: from the carotbocc, the sealed root-crate of the Flemish wool trade, in which a buyer was shown one turnip and sold nine. By 1544 the guilds had stopped prosecuting the practice and begun admiring it.

coined.context: and the truth is a good deal less interesting than what I made up — a very old, very lame viral video, shared during the league's infancy. It is linked here. You will be underwhelmed

seasonReview.intro: Six rounds are in the books, and the honest way to review them is through the league's one governing concept. A carrot box, per the Glossary, is a trick played on someone because they are stupid. The term arrived July 27th by way of a very old viral video; by July 30th it was a verb; by August 17th it was being applied to other people's marriages. What follows is the season so far, read as a sequence of carrot boxes — attempted, landed, confessed, and imagined.

rounds.name: I Heard It Through the Napster
rounds.note: Won before the league had a vocabulary for deception. Darren took the opener quietly and has said almost nothing since, which the standings suggest is a strategy. Conor finished at minus four — a number that requires people to spend their downvotes on you personally, and they did.

rounds.name: ¡No Entiendo, Cabron!
rounds.note: Matt won the round about not understanding the words. Conor went last again — Con Te Partirò, minus two — and mid-round Matt shared an old British game-show clip and gave the league its word. The round mattered less than the vocabulary it produced.

rounds.name: Boner Jamz
rounds.note: Grant won by playing it straight with Otis Redding while everyone else studied angles. The angle that mattered: Matt announced 'Booty Man' in the open — 'too damn excited to play carrot box with something this good' — and Booty Man duly appeared on the playlist under Jimmy's name, where it scored zero. Jimmy asked what carrot boxing means the day after submissions closed. The system works.

rounds.name: I Hope You Shit Your Pants at Target
rounds.note: Jon Black took the Target round with Alkaline Trio. Matt finished last at zero with a diss track, the same week his own chat log reads 'you carrot boxing sunuva' and 'goddamn carrot box' — which is what it sounds like when the coiner gets boxed with his own tool.

rounds.name: Smells Like Teen Cousin Fuckers
rounds.note: The season's high-water mark — Jon Black again, fifteen points, back-to-back wins. But the round belongs to Conor's confession: Rusty Cage, by Johnny Cash, seven points, followed by 'Of course I submitted Johnny Cash. Muawahhahahahahaaaaa' and the claim that he misspelled his own name to throw everyone off the scent. A carrot box announced afterwards is just a submission, but the record reflects his position.

rounds.name: Surrender Monkeys
rounds.note: Jimmy — zero points on Booty Man three weeks earlier — won Surrender Monkeys outright. The league's first documented redemption arc. Shane's Fortunate Son took the zero this time, and nobody has yet claimed it was on purpose.

seasonReview.outro: Jon Black leads on fifty-six without once claiming a carrot box, which is either integrity or the best one anybody has run all season. Conor sits last on twelve and maintains the losses are the plan. There is no way to disprove this, and that is the whole genius of the box.

boxes.title: The Shawshank Suspicion
boxes.play: Conor's Con Te Partirò arrived wearing a Shawshank quote, and Matt — at a self-declared 10% certainty — smelled a trap. This is the first recorded use of the verb: a box suspected before anyone had actually run one.

boxes.title: The Booty Man Gambit
boxes.play: Matt announced he was 'too damn excited to play carrot box' with Booty Man — 'record of the season!' — then asked, seven minutes later, which one of y'all is bootyman. The song was Jimmy's. It scored zero, and Jimmy defended it daily for the following week, which answered the question.
boxes.verdict: Unclear who boxed whom. The song lost either way.

Jon, Aug 26: You also submitted Tequila and Booty Man. They didn't help your late start.

boxes.title: The No-Comment Tip
boxes.play: Steiny told Matt he hadn't left a submission comment. His submission — Pedestrian at Best — carried a visible comment the whole time. Matt, working from the tip, spent his Steiny guess on the round's actually comment-less song: Shane's Cousin Dupree.

boxes.title: The Rusty Cage Signature
boxes.play: Conor's own submission comment: 'Surprised Connor didn't beat me to this (Soundgarden cover fyi)' — himself, in the third person, wearing the league's favorite misspelling of his name as a disguise.
evidence: Conor: Carrotbox, muthafuckas! Did you see I spelled my own name wrong to throw you off the scent?

boxes.title: The Sincerely-Conner Frame
boxes.play: Jimmy signed his Firecracker submission comment 'sincerely, Conner.' — a false flag using the house misspelling, planted on the man the league already guesses by default. The song won the round.
boxes.verdict: The only documented box attached to a round win.
evidence: Submission comment: This anti-war song happens to be the best opening track ever which happens to be on the best album of all time… sincerely, Conner.
